description: We are a team of enthusiastic students passionate about space exploration, science, and technology. We aim to build an interactive Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer that introduces young learners to astronaut training through engaging simulations, educational activities, and space-based challenges. Our goal is to make learning about space exciting, accessible, and fun!
summary: With The Lunar Mission, we wanted kids to feel what it is really like to run a base on the Moon. Our project addresses the “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer” challenge by turning NASA science into a game for ages 7 to 12. Players take care of an astronaut for 10 days, making decisions about life support, radiation, power and food. Every choice has consequences that show up later in the mission, helping kids understand that one small decision can change the whole outcome. It’s designed for use in classrooms, libraries, and outreach programs.
details:
The Lunar Mission is a browser-based game set on a lunar base. Over 10 days, the player faces real challenges of living on the Moon: a broken water recycler, a solar storm, stuffy air, a power cut, and the long, freezing Moon night. Each day, the astronaut acts out the player’s choice, and an End Mission Analysis explains how earlier decisions shaped the result. Simple words and short definitions keep the science easy for young learners.
Tech Stack
HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript
Responsive Web Layout
Google Fonts: Orbitron, Michroma
Backgrounds designed in Figma
Ready for deployment via Netlify
Innovation Highlights
Learning by Doing: Kids decide, drag and click instead of answering quiz questions.
Connected Consequences: Early choices change later days, showing how a base works as one system.
Data Trust: Real NASA information and made-up game values are clearly labelled.
Visual Simplicity: Clear text, friendly characters and a calm space theme.
